claims.subject: question (a): 0x008BD720 thunk dispatch
claims.statement: The complete body of 0x008BD720 is exactly two instructions: LEA EAX,[ECX+0x18] (VA 0x008BD720) followed by RET (VA 0x008BD723). It contains NO jump and NO call. There is NO dispatch target VA: the function does not transfer control anywhere except back to its caller.
claims.answer_to_question_a: NO dispatch target exists. The premise 'callback thunk dispatches to a target' is rejected. The body is a leaf that returns the interior pointer ECX+0x18 in EAX.
evidence: EXTRACT_SUBREGION_A_008BD720_008BD740.txt rows 1-2 (source lines 1282626-1282627; VA 008BD720 LEA EAX,[ECX + 0x18]; VA 008BD723 RET)
Direct source re-read cross-check (Read tool, source lines 1282626-1282629) - extract is verbatim

Body completeness: RET at 0x008BD723 terminates the body; next listed instruction in window is 0x008BD730 (a separate body, INCIDENT-P06-I1); no JMP/CALL instruction exists anywhere in the admitted window A
premises: The pinned listing (SHA256 642CC29A...CC1D8DB, verified twice) is the frozen scientific corpus for this package
RET terminates the basic block; the body cannot 'continue' after RET
VA-delta consistency: LEA (3 bytes) + RET (1 byte) ends at 0x008BD724; gap to 0x008BD730 is consistent with inter-body padding, not with hidden instructions
claims.countermodel_considered: A dispatch could hide after RET or in the 0x008BD724-0x008BD72F gap: rejected - the window contains no listed instruction there, and any real thunk would need a JMP/CALL instruction inside its own body; the body as listed contains none. The gap bytes are not listed in the corpus; treating them as hidden code would be speculation outside saved evidence.
claims.claim_resolution: REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE (the dispatch premise); ANSWERED (the question: target VA = NONE)

claims.subject: question (a): operational meaning of 0x008BD720 as the pinned {0x66,A} request callback
claims.statement: When invoked, 0x008BD720 computes EAX = ECX + 0x18 and returns. As the pinned request callback it yields the address of the +0x18 sub-object/field of whatever object the scheduler passes in ECX. The continuation of the {0x66,A} chain therefore lies CONSUMER-SIDE: in the code that invokes this callback and uses the returned pointer (22 direct CALL sites and 3 imm32 registration-shaped sites exist in the pinned listing), and/or in the +0x18 sub-object itself - not in any callee of 0x008BD720 (it has none).
evidence: CLAIM-P06-C1 body semantics (register-pure, unconditional, no memory access)
Bridge standing (cited, not re-derived): 0x008BD720 pinned as the {0x66,A} request's callback via imm32 - DRAFT_FINAL_REPORT.md L185-186, HANDOFF.md L16, PE_MASTER_REVIEW.md L29

Navigation-only address search in the pinned listing (no caller region read): 22 direct CALL sites (0054F7BB, 0055000F, 00556FAD, 00556FC5, 00557030, 00557912, 0055792A, 0055794E, 005CB73A, 006B1E5A, 006B6DB9, 006C88C6, 006C88D5, 006D3BAE, 006D3BC8, 006D3BD7, 006D3CD6, 006D3CFE, 006D3D26, 006D3D3A, 006D4441, 006E68A8) and 3 imm32 load sites (006B6D05 MOV EBX,0x8bd720; 006C3FB0 MOV EBX,0x8bd720; 006D44E8 MOV EDI,0x8bd720)
premises: Bridge premise inherited (cited): ECX at callback invocation is the request/scheduler-side object; NOT re-derived here
Premise preserved: 'no direct caller != exclusively virtual' - 0x008BD720 has 22 direct callers AND is address-taken (3 imm32 sites in listing), so it is NOT exclusively virtual
Data-section (vtable) references are not visible in the instruction listing; absence in-listing is not proof of absence in binary
claims.countermodel_considered: The callback imm32 might be stored as data and never invoked, or invoked with a different register convention. Neither changes the in-window fact: the body is register-pure pointer arithmetic and cannot dispatch. If the callback is invoked, its whole observable effect is 'return &arg+0x18'.
claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (body semantics and register-purity); NOT_ESTABLISHED (which caller/registration site is the {0x66,A} scheduler, and what the +0x18 sub-object is)
claims.claim_resolution: CONDITIONAL on the inherited bridge premise; the experiment-design consequence is unconditional: the bridge's designed step 'decode FUN_008BD720 and the type-0x66 provider chain' cannot continue through a callee - it must continue through the consumer/registration side.

claims.subject: question (b): flag-dispatch structure of 0x00848EA0
claims.statement: 0x00848EA0 begins with an MSVC SEH prologue (PUSH -0x1; PUSH handler 0x00A28300; MOV EAX,FS:[0x0]; ...; MOV FS:[0x0],EAX), loads its first stack argument into EDI (MOV EDI,[ESP+0x80]) and queries it: PUSH 0x1; MOV ECX,EDI; CALL 0x00745540; TEST AL,AL; MOV ECX,EDI; JZ 0x00848FEC. Non-zero result (flag 1 TRUE) falls through into the in-window lookup/compose chain; zero result jumps OUT of the window to 0x00848FEC. This instruction-level confirms the bridge's AMEND-4/AMEND-5 corrected standing that the lerp chain executes under FUN_00745540(1)!=0, and locates the flag-2 path (per bridge: the per-slot {u16@+0xC, float@+0x10} stores) at >= 0x00848FEC, i.e. OUTSIDE this admitted window.

JZ target 0x00848FEC > window end 0x00848FC4-exclusive: recorded VA, NOT read

claims.subject: question (b): slot-object interface and class semantics
claims.statement: The slot(-container) object consumed by 0x00848EA0 is its FIRST STACK ARGUMENT (MOV EDI,[ESP+0x80]; the function is not thiscall-on-the-slot - it receives the object by stack and then uses it as 'this' by loading ECX=EDI before each method call). In-window it uses exactly three direct (non-virtual in-window) methods on this object, all in the 0x00745xxx family: (1) 0x00745540(this,1) -> boolean AL (kind-of-slot predicate); (2) 0x00745BF0(this) -> pointer EAX, null-checked with TEST EAX,EAX + JZ 0x00848FC6 early exit (this is the in-window entry point of the bridge's id2/property channel); (3) 0x00745690(this,0) -> x87 float returned in st0 and consumed via PUSH ECX;FSTP [ESP]. In-window 0x00848EA0 performs NO direct object-field read: every field access is delegated to these callees or lives on the out-of-window flag-2 path. The slot object's CLASS is NOT established in-window (no vtable dereference, no RTTI, no constructor visible).
evidence: EXTRACT_SUBREGION_B rows: arg load (1145817), flag query (1145820-1145822), null-checked getter (1145824-1145833), float getter + st0 consume idiom (1145871-1145875)
Direct-call (static target) form of all three CALLs - no CALL [reg]/CALL EDX dispatch in-window

Exhaustive in-window direct-dereference census: [ESP+0x80] (arg), [0x00A7B25C] (float const), [0x00B9D8D0] (MSVC security cookie), FS:[0x0] (SEH chain), [EAX]/[EAX+0x4]/[EAX+0x8] (the 0x006C1F90 result triple); NO other memory read in-window
premises: Idiom-level return interpretation (TEST AL,AL=boolean; TEST EAX,EAX=null-check; PUSH ECX+FSTP [ESP] immediately after CALL=x87 st0 float return) - x86/MSVC conventions, strongly supported, not byte-proven

Premise preserved: identical lookup shapes or parameter names do not prove common semantics - the 0x00745xxx family shape suggests one class but does NOT establish the bridge's class-20006 attribution
claims.countermodel_considered: (a) The 0x745xxx entries might be free functions that merely take ECX by convention - possible in principle; in-window they are this-called on EDI (the slot object), so at minimum they form the slot object's in-window interface. (b) AL/EAX/st0 might carry non-bool/non-ptr/non-float values - does not change the interface shape. (c) The class-20006 property tag 6 hypothesis: UNVERIFIED in-window - the property read is inside 0x00745BF0 and deeper callees (not admitted). This package neither confirms nor refutes it.
claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (call structure, this-object wiring, no-direct-field-read census); STRONGLY_SUPPORTED (return-type idioms); NOT_ESTABLISHED (slot object class identity)
claims.claim_resolution: ANSWERED (interface semantics); NOT_ESTABLISHED (class identity); UNVERIFIED (class-20006/tag-6 hypothesis - outside window)

claims.statement: In-window flag-1 chain: P = 0x00745BF0(slot); L = 0x00843D60(&frame5C, P); obj1 = 0x00844660(L); obj2 = 0x0043A550(obj1); EBP = 0x0072F580(obj2) [the bridge's keyed-lookup chain, cited]; the lookup chain is exception-guarded (MSVC __try: local trylevel [ESP+0x78] set 0 before 0x00844660->0x0043A550->0x0072F580 and -1 after; SEH handler imm 0x00A28300 recorded, NOT read); a frame local at [ESP+0x58] is passed to 0x008E0110 (callee, NOT read); guard 0x0072FCE0(EBP) -> boolean (FALSE -> JZ 0x00848FC4, outside window); 0x0072FE30(EBP, buf1, buf2, buf3) fills three 12-byte float3 frame buffers that were zero-initialized in-window (FLDZ + 7 FST/FSTP stores) - out-parameter idiom; t = 0x00745690(slot, 0) -> float; R = 0x006C1F90(ptr_a, ptr_b, ptr_c, t) (4 cdecl dwords, caller-cleans via ADD ESP,0x10) -> EAX -> 12-byte float triple ([EAX], [EAX+4], [EAX+8]) copied into frame locals; JMP 0x00848FC6 (epilogue, outside window). The bridge's semantic labels ('lookup', 'lerp', 'store to slot+0x00', 'R08 loop over 3 slots') are inherited standing from their full-body C3 decompile (cited); the store-to-slot+0x00 and the loop are NOT in this window (they lie in the epilogue/flag-2 regions >= 0x00848FC4/0x00848FEC).

claims.subject: question (b): FAMILY-P/T merge - does any VFS-record-fed channel reach 0x00848EA0 in-window?
claims.statement: NO. In-window, no VFS-record-fed channel reaches 0x00848EA0's data flow. The complete in-window data-source census: (1) the stack argument arg1 (slot object) - provenance is the single in-listing direct caller 0x004E55F7 (CALL 0x00848ea0), NOT read; (2) float constant [0x00A7B25C] (.data static); (3) MSVC security cookie [0x00B9D8D0]; (4) FS:[0] SEH chain; (5) return values of the 11 direct callees (all outside the admitted window). No file/registry/record-reader call, no record-array dereference, and no VFS handle appears in-window. This is a SCOPED negative: it does NOT prove end-to-end absence - a VFS-fed channel, if real, enters through (i) the id2/property provenance inside 0x00745BF0 and its callees (the class-20006 tag-6 read), (ii) the class-20006 property-tag-6 WRITERS (bridge proposal), or (iii) the arg1 slot-object provenance at caller 0x004E55F7.
evidence: Exhaustive CALL census in-window: 11 direct CALLs with static targets (0x00745540, 0x00745BF0, 0x00843D60, 0x00844660, 0x0043A550, 0x0072F580, 0x008E0110, 0x0072FCE0, 0x0072FE30, 0x00745690, 0x006C1F90); zero indirect calls in-window
Exhaustive direct-dereference census (as in CLAIM-P06-C4)

premises: Scoped-negative discipline: the claim is about IN-WINDOW visibility only

Bridge standing (cited, DRAFT_FINAL_REPORT L172-178): within the censused construction machinery, drivers' inputs come from message dispatch, runtime attributes, or hardcoded immediates; templates.vfs is consumed as a DEFINITION registry only; the only file reader is the registry loader with census 1 caller

claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (in-window visibility negative); NOT_ESTABLISHED (end-to-end merge question)
claims.claim_resolution: SCOPED ANSWER: merge NOT decidable in-window; exact gap edges recorded (0x00745BF0 property provenance; class-20006 tag-6 writers; caller 0x004E55F7)
